title: Adopt variant C as the shipping runtime, with a regenerable digit mapping
spec: Spawned by T-6's ruling (kb/wiki/decision-t6-correctness-rerun.md). Replace the xpr runtime's string-coercion branch with variant C, proven at spikes/T-6/runtime-variantC.sql: after the ASCII numeric gate fails, btrim with Python's full 29-code-point isspace set and translate the 670 non-ASCII Nd code points onto 0-9, then re-test. Measured: 0 wrong numbers at efd 1 over 11,367 expressions, 0 refusals, fixture 130/130, 812ms vs an 852ms baseline per 300k ordinary coercions. THE NESTING IS LOAD-BEARING: hoisting translate() above the ASCII gate costs 5.3x (4553ms) because every ordinary numeric string then pays it, and T-5 found every number-declared field in the tenant project is stored as text. Keep the comment that says so. ALSO IN SCOPE: the 670-character mapping is generated from Python's unicodedata, not hand-written, so add the generator to the build and a test that fails when the installed mapping disagrees with the running Python's Nd set - a Unicode version bump must not silently desync the two engines. Variant A (the named refusal, spikes/T-6/runtime.sql) stays committed as the one-line reversal if Evan overturns the deviation.
